name: What documents and information should I gather before meeting an addition contractor?

mainEntity.name: What documents and information should I gather before meeting an addition contractor?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Bring basic property information and a clear wish list so the contractor can give you useful feedback. You don’t need detailed plans yet, but more clarity upfront leads to better guidance.

Contractors can’t give solid estimates without at least rough dimensions and constraints. Being prepared makes your meetings more productive and accurate.

Key factors:
- Any existing plans, surveys, or past permits if you have them
- Rough measurements or a sketch of your current layout
- Photos of the house, lot, and any problem areas
- A prioritized list of needs, wants, and nice‑to‑haves

Spend an evening measuring key rooms and sketching the general layout. Bring printed photos and a rough budget range; this lets the contractor quickly confirm what’s realistic and what might need to be scaled or phased.
acceptedAnswer.description: Gather any existing plans, surveys, and past permit paperwork, plus rough measurements and photos of your home. Bring a prioritized wish list and a realistic budget range. This gives the contractor enough information to discuss feasible options, rough costs, and next steps during your first meeting.
